definitions.explanation: Devoting oneself exclusively to one type of work or business, without a side job or other occupation.

examples.japanese: {専業|せんぎょう}{主婦|しゅふ}になった。
{専業|せんぎょう}{農家|のうか}として{米|こめ}を{作|つく}っている。
examples.english: He grows rice as a full-time farmer.

examples.japanese: {副業|ふくぎょう}をやめて、{本業|ほんぎょう}を{専業|せんぎょう}にすることにした。
examples.english: I decided to quit my side job and focus solely on my main business.

notes:
USAGE:
{専業|せんぎょう} is most commonly used as a modifier before a noun, especially in the compounds {専業|せんぎょう}{主婦|しゅふ} (full-time housewife) and {専業|せんぎょう}{農家|のうか} (full-time farmer). It contrasts with {兼業|けんぎょう} (side business; holding multiple jobs).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {専業|せんぎょう}{主婦|しゅふ} (full-time housewife)
- {専業|せんぎょう}{主夫|しゅふ} (full-time househusband)
- {専業|せんぎょう}{農家|のうか} (full-time farming household)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{兼業|けんぎょう} (side business; working in multiple occupations) is the antonym.
